name: CEPF Mediterranean Basin Biodiversity Hotspot grants
summary: CEPF small and large grants for civil society organisations protecting freshwater, coastal and traditionally managed landscapes and threatened plants in eligible Mediterranean Basin countries, with BirdLife International as regional implementation team.
reporting: Large-grant holders file financial reports every quarter and progress reports every six months through CEPF’s online system.

eligibility.rule: The project supports at least one strategic direction in the ecosystem profile
Has its own bank account and is legally authorized to receive grants
No child or forced labor, large or complex dams, government security salaries, firearms or other weapons
Project does not resettle people or purchase land
Project does not introduce or use potentially invasive, non-indigenous species
Project does not remove or alter tangible cultural heritage
Project has no potential to harm critical habitat

applicant_types.quote: invite civil society organizations to apply for small grants in the Mediterranean Basin Biodiversity Hotspot

geography.quote: Eligible Countries Albania, Algeria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Cabo Verde, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Montenegro, Morocco, North Macedonia, Palestine, Tunisia

access.quote: Applicants are invited to submit their LOI online via the ConservationGrants portal in French or English.

window.quote: Applications submitted after the deadline will not be accepted whatever the reason.

reporting.quote: Recipients of large grants must submit financial reports each quarter and progress reports every six months through ConservationGrants.

eligibility.quote: The project must also support at least one strategic direction outlined in the CEPF ecosystem profile for the hotspot.
Organizations must have their own bank account and be authorized under relevant national laws to receive charitable contributions.

CEPF does not fund the following activities: Use of child labor or forced labor. Construction or rehabilitation of large or complex dams. Payment of salaries or salary supplements to government security personnel. Purchase of firearms or other weapons.
Physical resettlement of people (voluntary or involuntary). Purchase of land.
Activities that introduce or use potentially invasive, non-indigenous species.
Removal or alteration of any tangible cultural heritage.
Activities that have the potential to cause adverse impacts to critical habitat.

effort.quote: Large-grant applicants submit letters of inquiry online, through the online grants database ConservationGrants. Small-grant applicants submit letters of inquiry using an offline template that will be provided in the open call instructions.

These applicants will have a defined period of time (typically around two months, although this may vary among hotspots) to submit a complete project proposal through the online portal ConservationGrants.
If a project triggers one or more safeguard policies, the grantee will be asked to prepare the relevant safeguard document(s) and incorporate related measures into the project's design.

after_award.quote: Recipients of large grants must submit financial reports each quarter and progress reports every six months through ConservationGrants.
Large-grant recipients are required to attend a CEPF online orientation training within the first three months of their project's start date.
